div.head: V Atr 32.4
div.ab: ⁊ be norðan stod seo unlagu, þæt man moste banweorc on unsacne secgan; ⁊ þæt scolde standan, gif hit wurde swa gecyðed ydæges sona.

⁊ be norðan stod seo unlagu, þæt man moste banweorc on unsacne secgan, ⁊ þæt scolde standan, gif hit wurde swa gecyðed ydæges sona.
And be norðan stod seo unlagu þæt man moste banweorc on unsacne secgan, and þæt scolde standan gif hit wurde swa gecyðed ydæges sona.

Und im Norden galt der Rechtsmissbrauch, dass man gegen einen Unschuldigen Todtschlag aussagen durfte, und diese [Aussage als erwiesen] gelten sollte, wenn sie so alsbald am Tage [des Todtschlags] selbst erklärt wurde.
And in the north there was the abuse that one could charge an innocent man with a killing, and that [charge] was to stand [as proven] if it was declared at once on the same day [as the killing].

And in the north there has prevailed the unjust practice of bringing accusations of homicide against a guiltless man, and such an accusation was held to be valid, if it was made at once on the very day [of the homicide].
And in the North the abuse was current, that homicide might be laid to the charge of a guiltless person, and that should be held valid if it were announced thus at once on the same day.

And in the north there has been the unlawful practice that one can level an accusation of murder against an innocent person and it shall be permitted to stand if it was made immediately on the same day.

note.seg: Das Wort fehlt Wbb. Erklärung aus bán ‘Knochen’ oder bann ist unmöglich. Im Agsä. heisst zwar bana nur ‘Mörder, Totschläger’; dagegen mengl. ban(e) daneben: ‘Verderben, Tod, Totschlag’ (wie mhd., nord.). Und Sweet erklärt aus diesem Sinne: bangar ‘tödlicher Speer’, bansnaca [dagegen Toller Suppl.: bán-] ‘Giftschlange’.—Der Missbrauch besteht in der zu weiten Ausdehnung der Notorietät, die dem Kläger Beweisnähe verleiht und Beklagten in den aus Handhaftigkeit (s. d. Gl 7) folgenden Rechtsnachteil versetzt, sich nicht verteidigen zu dürfen; vgl. Gl Kundmachung 4

The word is missing from the dictionaries. An explanation from bán ‘bone’ or from bann is impossible. In A.-S., it is true, bana means only ‘murderer, slayer’; but Middle English ban(e) also has, alongside this, the sense ‘ruin, death, killing’ (as in Middle High German and Norse). And Sweet explains from this sense: bangar ‘deadly spear’, bansnaca [against this Toller Suppl.: bán-] ‘poisonous snake’.—The abuse consists in extending notoriety too far, which gives the plaintiff the nearer right to proof and places the defendant under the legal disadvantage that follows from being taken in the act (see that word in Gl 7), namely that he may not defend himself; cf. Gl Kundmachung 4
